confirmed.title: Superconducting accumulator and coil capacitor show vanilla (untinted) colour whenever they charge or discharge
confirmed.evidence:
kinds.accumulator (line 81) tints only chargable_graphics.picture. kinds.capacitor (lines 89-91) tints picture but uses plain accumulator_charge() / accumulator_discharge(). The charge/discharge animations are not light overlays: /opt/factorio/data/base/prototypes/entity/entities.lua:159 and :198 make layer 1 of each the full body, accumulator_picture({1, 1, 1, 1}, 24); only layer 2 is the draw_as_glow overlay. The engine shows charge_animation/discharge_animation while charging or discharging (vanilla puts the whole body in them for that reason, entities.lua:5301-5307).
The data.raw dump (scratch dumper mod, `python3 .../review/dump.py base`, then leaves.py) shows both entities with 'chargable_graphics accumulator.png tint=[1, 1, 1, 1] x2' next to the one tinted picture leaf. So the tint is visible only when the accumulator is idle (full with no demand, or empty).
FINAL_SPEC.md:301 says the opposite ('charge/discharge animations are light overlays, untouched'). Test S12 only requires at least one tinted leaf, so it passes.
confirmed.fix: Tint the whole chargable_graphics: U.tint(e.chargable_graphics, spec.tint) in kinds.accumulator, and the same on g after building it in kinds.capacitor. The walker already skips the draw_as_shadow and draw_as_glow layers. Or pass the tint into the body layers of charge_animation.layers[1] and discharge_animation.layers[1]. Correct FINAL_SPEC.md:301, and extend S12 to require the tint on every non-glow, non-shadow accumulator.png leaf.

confirmed.title: Space Age: tint walker colours the maglev underground belt's frost overlays (frozen_patch_in / frozen_patch_out)
confirmed.evidence:
The SKIP table (util.lua:23-24) has frozen_patch but not frozen_patch_in or frozen_patch_out, the keys SA uses inside underground-belt `structure`.
SA dump (`python3 .../review/dump.py sa`) shows 'magnetics-maglev-underground-belt .structure.frozen_patch_in.sheet __space-age__/graphics/entity/frozen/underground-belt/underground-belt-structure.png [0.9, 0.62, 1, 1]', and the same for frozen_patch_out. The belt's and splitter's own frozen_patch leaves stay untinted.
The entity really can freeze: Aquilo has magnetic-field = 10 (space-age/prototypes/planet/planet.lua:629), which meets the min-10 surface condition, and the underground needs heating_energy 250 kW. So the frost on Aquilo is drawn purple/pink.
Test S12 copies the same skip list (tools/tests.py:657 SKIP_KEYS), so it validates the walker against itself and passes.
confirmed.fix: Skip every key that starts with 'frozen_patch' in U.tint, for example `if not SKIP[k] and not (type(k) == 'string' and k:find('^frozen_patch'))`, and mirror that in tests.py SKIP_KEYS.

The walker therefore reaches `structure.frozen_patch_in.sheet` and `structure.frozen_patch_out.sheet`, which have a `filename`, and sets their tint.

3. **A fresh dump confirms it.** I regenerated the Space Age dump myself (sk1_dump.py, a copy of dump.py writing to sk1dump_sa.json). frozen_patch = true, frozen_patch_in = true, frozen_patch_out = true, ...

- Add 'frozen_patch_in' and 'frozen_patch_out' to `SKIP_KEYS`.
- If you use the substring rule, change `walk_ctx` to skip when `isinstance(k, str) and 'frozen' in k`.

Then add an S12 check that the maglev underground's `structure.frozen_patch_in.sheet` and `structure.frozen_patch_out.sheet` have no tint in the Space Age configuration, i.e. the same tint as express-underground-belt (none).

- each of these must be flagged: `if not mods["space-age"] then "foundry"`, `if not SA then "turbo-transport-belt"`, `if U.SA == false then "electromagnetic-plant"`, `if mods["space-age"] == nil then "foundry"`, `if x or SA then "foundry"`

A prototype of this logic (scratchpad/review/s8fix.py) passes all 10 probe cases, including the existing self-check, and gives 0 hits on the current mod, so S8 stays green.

- `if U.SA == false then ... "electromagnetic-plant"` returned [].

split.title: Under Space Age, 'Air liquefaction' (no inputs → 50 LN2) also runs on space platforms (pressure 0), and SC cable and flux-crystal growth can be made in space
split.evidence: Only recipes with sa_magnetic_field_min get surface_conditions (recipes.lua:24-26; spec.py:100 has none for magnetics-liquid-nitrogen). data-updates.lua:30-32 adds magnetics-cryogenics to the SA cryogenic plant. An SA prototype dump (scratchpad dump_sa.json) shows cryogenic-plant surface_conditions = nil and categories including 'magnetics-cryogenics'. A cryogenic plant on a platform can therefore 'liquefy air' in vacuum and also run SC cable and flux-crystal growth. This undercuts §7.3, which puts all 26 Magnetics entities planet-side (magnetic-field ≥ 10, platform = 0). I took this from the prototypes; I did not run it on a real platform.
split.fix: Under SA, give magnetics-liquid-nitrogen surface_conditions {pressure, min = 10}, or {magnetic-field, min = 10} to match the rest of the mod. Optionally do the same for the growth recipe if flux crystals are meant to stay planet-side.

votes.reasoning:
I tried to refute this finding and could not. I confirmed it on the 2.0.77 headless server with Space Age. I used a scratch probe mod in the scratchpad (review/probe_ln2) and changed nothing in the project.

Static evidence:
- recipes.lua:24-26 sets surface_conditions only when `d.sa_magnetic_field_min` is present. In spec.py:100-103, magnetics-liquid-nitrogen has `ing=[]` and no such field. Only stone-separation has it (spec.py:113).
- data-updates.lua:27,30-33 adds magnetics-cryogenics to the SA cryogenic-plant.
- In vanilla space-age/prototypes/entity/entities.lua, cryogenic-plant has no surface_conditions.
- space-age/prototypes/surface.lua gives the space-platform surface pressure = 0 and magnetic-field = 0.

Runtime evidence (python3 run.run('sa', 1000, with_tests=False, extra_mods=[probe])):
- I created a real platform with `create_space_platform` and `apply_starter_pack`. On surface platform-1: pressure=0, mf=0.
- can_place cryogenic-plant = true. can_place magnetics-cryo-chamber = false, which is the control: E8 works for entities.
- The LN2 recipe's surface_conditions = nil. The plant's categories include magnetics-cryogenics.
- After 900 ticks: products_finished=6, fluidbox = 300 magnetics-liquid-nitrogen, status full_output. So "Air liquefaction" produces LN2 from nothing in vacuum.

Why I still call it a defect even though the code follows the spec text:
- §7.1 (FINAL_SPEC.md:127) says "SA platform balance is untouched by construction (test E8)". §7.3 calls Magnetics hardware "planet-side".
- That guarantee covers only placing Magnetics entities. The category insert into the SA cryogenic plant, which works on platforms, is not covered by it.
- The fluid's own description says "Liquefied from air in the cryo chamber". Running it in vacuum contradicts that.
- Test S8 (tools/magnetics-tests/cells/static.lua:977-981) requires every recipe except stone-separation to have an empty surface_conditions. That test locks the gap in place; it does not catch it.
- §15 does not address this.

Severity: I would argue it down from a balance problem to a consistency problem. The real balance effect is close to zero:
- Everything that consumes SC cable or flux crystals is a planet-only Magnetics entity, or ammo for planet-only turrets.
- Making cable or crystals in orbit requires launching magnet alloy, plastic, processing units and U-238 to the platform.
- The real defects are a physically absurd recipe (air liquefaction in vacuum) and a false guarantee in the spec. "minor" is the right severity, or lower.

A nuance on the fix: LN2 and ferrofluid both have auto_barrel = false (magnetics/prototypes/fluids.lua:6), so neither fluid can be shipped by rocket. If LN2 can no longer be made on platforms, SC cable and flux-crystal growth are also impossible there. There is no need to condition those two recipes separately.

A second nuance, from a second probe (probe2): I set the LN2 recipe's condition to pressure ≥ 10 in data-final-fixes. The plant still produced 300 LN2 (6 crafts) after a script `set_recipe`. The engine checks recipe surface conditions only when a recipe is chosen through the GUI, not when it is set by script. This is the same limitation §15.3/E9 already records for stone-separation. So any test for the fix has to be static (S8), not a runtime check through `set_recipe`.
votes.fix:
Under Space Age, give only the Air liquefaction recipe an atmosphere condition. Use {property = "pressure", min = 10}: this is "needs air", the same rule the kiln and the MHD generator already use in §7.3. Every planet stays allowed (Aquilo 300, Fulgora 800, Nauvis 1000, Gleba 2000, Vulcanus 4000). Space platforms (pressure 0) are blocked. Steps:

(1) spec.py:100, add `sa_pressure_min=10` to magnetics-liquid-nitrogen.

(2) recipes.lua:24-26, build the list from both fields:
`local sc = {}`
`if d.sa_magnetic_field_min then sc[#sc+1] = {property="magnetic-field", min=d.sa_magnetic_field_min} end`
`if d.sa_pressure_min then sc[#sc+1] = {property="pressure", min=d.sa_pressure_min} end`
`if U.SA and #sc > 0 then r.surface_conditions = sc end`

(3) Do not condition SC cable or flux-crystal growth. LN2 has auto_barrel = false and cannot be shipped, so blocking its source keeps the whole cryogenics chain on planets.

(4) Update test S8 (cells/static.lua:979) so that magnetics-liquid-nitrogen expects {pressure ≥ 10}. Keep the base-game branch expecting no conditions.

(5) Record the change in FINAL_SPEC §15.1 (the §7.3 table and §7.1 line 127 must not be rewritten). Note there that the engine enforces recipe surface conditions only when a recipe is chosen through the GUI; a script `set_recipe` bypasses them, as already recorded for E9. Do not add a runtime test that relies on `set_recipe`.

Regenerate spec_data.lua with spec.py and rerun tools/tests.py.

votes.reasoning:
The facts in the finding are right, but they are not a balance defect, and they do not depart from the spec.

1. **The facts check out.** Under Space Age, `recipes.lua:24-26` adds surface_conditions only to recipes that have `sa_magnetic_field_min`. Only stone-separation has it (`spec.py:113`). `magnetics-liquid-nitrogen` has no inputs (`spec.py:100`). `data-updates.lua:30-32` puts `magnetics-cryogenics` on the SA cryogenic plant. The vanilla cryogenic-plant block (`/opt/factorio/data/space-age/prototypes/entity/entities.lua` ~1949-2100) has no surface_conditions. So a cryogenic plant on a platform can make LN2, SC cable and grown crystals.

2. **The spec asks for this, and a test enforces it.** §1.4 says the cryogenic plant "gets magnetics-cryogenics". §7.2 item 2 whitelists the category inserts on the EM plant, cryogenic plant and foundry. §7.3 restricts the 26 Magnetics *entities*, and stone-separation is the only *recipe* it restricts. §15 changes none of this. Test S8 (`tools/magnetics-tests/cells/static.lua:977-981`) asserts that every Magnetics recipe except stone-separation has *empty* surface_conditions under SA. The proposed fix would therefore break S8 and go against §7.3. The SA cryogenic plant is a vanilla entity, not one of the 26, so "all 26 Magnetics entities planet-side" still holds.

3. **Balance is not affected.**
   - LN2 costs nothing on every planet, so making it in space adds no resource.
   - Nothing made this way can be used on a platform:
     - SC cable and crystals feed Magnetics buildings, and every one of them is blocked at magnetic-field 0 (E8).
     - Crystal charging needs the resonator, which is also blocked.
     - Magnetics ammo uses Magnetics-only ammo categories (`magnetics-slug`, `-gauss`, `-rail`; `spec.py:45-65`, 310-331), which only the blocked Magnetics turrets accept.
   - Making these in space is strictly worse than on the ground. No asteroid gives stone, so ferrite and magnet alloy must be shipped up. Planets already produce the same outputs with no surface limit.
   - So "SA platform balance untouched" (§1.4) still holds: a platform gains no new ability.

4. **What is left is flavour.** Air liquefaction in vacuum reads oddly, and the LN2 description says it is "liquefied from air in the cryo chamber". That is a theme mismatch, not a balance or code defect.

If the author wants to fix the theme anyway, three changes go together. Add `{property = "pressure", min = 10}` to `magnetics-liquid-nitrogen` only, under SA. Add that recipe to §7.3 as a new §15 entry. Update the S8 expectation to match. Every planet has pressure ≥ 10, so only platforms would be affected. SC cable and growth are then blocked in space as well, because they need LN2 piped in and fluids cannot be shipped.

split.title: RU: «Катушечник» (разг. — катушечный магнитофон) и «Разрядник» (устройство защиты от перенапряжений) — неестественные имена турелей
split.evidence: ru:64 `magnetics-coilgun-turret=Катушечник`, ru:106 tech «Катушечник», ru:27-28 «Боеприпас катушечника», ru:136 категория «Болванки катушечника»; ru:66 и :112 `Разрядник`. votes.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. It is a real minor defect in the Russian text, though one of its supporting arguments is weaker than it claims.

What I checked:
- **The quoted lines are correct.** In magnetics/locale/ru/magnetics.cfg: line 64 `magnetics-coilgun-turret=Катушечник`, line 66 `magnetics-arc-emitter=Разрядник`, technology names at 106 and 112, ammo descriptions at 27–28, and the ammo category `Болванки катушечника` at 136.
- **The source is spec.py.** The same strings are at tools/spec.py lines 314, 328, 351, 365, 49, 54 and 72, and FINAL_SPEC §9 repeats them at lines 736, 737, 770, 772, 783, 794 and 800.
- **No design reason is given.** FINAL_SPEC, design_appeal.md and judges.json never explain why these Russian names were chosen. §15 does not change them.
- **The vanilla citations are correct.** base.cfg:378 has `Пулемётная турель` and :398 has `Лазерная турель`. space-age.cfg:362 has `Рельсотронная турель` and :386 has `Тесла-турель`. Vanilla technologies take the entity name in the singular: base.cfg:1144 `gun-turret=Пулемётная турель`, :1153 `laser-turret=Лазерная турель`.

Where the finding overstates:
- **Not every vanilla turret is a "…турель".** The artillery turret is `Артиллерийское орудие` (base.cfg:270). The mod's own `Пушка Гаусса` and `Рельсовая пушка` are fine because «пушка» already says "weapon". So the real problem is narrower than breaking a naming pattern.
- **The real problem:** these are the only two of the mod's four turrets whose names do not say "weapon", and both words already have common everyday meanings:
  - «катушечник» is common slang for a reel-to-reel tape recorder;
  - «разрядник» is an electrical protection device (spark gap or surge arrester), and also the everyday word for an athlete with a sports grade.
- **The ammo text inherits it.** «Болванки катушечника» in the bonus screen and «Боеприпас катушечника» in the ammo descriptions read as "ammo of the tape recorder".
- **«Разрядник» is the weaker half.** In an electric theme it at least suggests discharges, and the entity description («Цепная молния…») gives context. It is still ambiguous and does not say it is a turret.
- **I could not check a dictionary.** Wiktionary is blocked by the egress proxy, so the everyday meanings above are common Russian usage, not a cited source.
- **Severity stays minor.** This is localisation quality only. No tests pin these Russian strings: grep finds them only in spec.py, locale, FINAL_SPEC, and comments in items.lua:1, entities.lua:2 and report.py:38,40.

One correction to the proposed fix: vanilla technology names are the singular entity name, not a plural, so the technology should be «Катушечная турель», not «Катушечные турели».

votes.reasoning:
This is a matter of taste about deliberately chosen names. It is not a concrete defect, and half of the finding's evidence does not hold up.

1. The names are a spec decision that the tests enforce, not a translation slip. FINAL_SPEC.md §9.2 and §9.4 set these names on purpose: line 770 «Coilgun | Катушечник | Spulenkanone», line 772 «Arc emitter | Разрядник | Bogenstrahler», plus lines 736–737, 783, 794 and 800. §15 (post-pilot changes) does not touch them. Test S11 parses §9 and requires the cfg values and the game's `--dump-prototype-locale` output to equal those names exactly (tests.py:429-444, :1005, :1028-1030). split.title: T-W 'SC-wall share ≤ ½ of stone share' cannot fail: SC walls with zero resistances still pass
split.evidence: combat.lua:818 and 835-837 compare the share lost = lost / (160 × max_health). With 1500 vs 350 HP, the check passes whenever lost_sc ≤ 1500/700 × lost_stone = 2.14 × lost_stone. So SC walls may lose more absolute HP than stone walls and still pass. Mutation A set the SC wall and gate resistances to 0/0 for every damage type. All 5 T-W SC checks still passed. Coilgun: SC lost 2655.0 vs stone 2384.4, check 0.01106 ≤ 0.02129. Gauss: 900.0 vs 748.4. Only W1, S4 and K10 caught the mutation. The criterion change itself is accepted in §15.2. Note that with the committed data, the original absolute criterion would fail for coilgun (1136.2 > 2005.6/2) and gauss (447.9 > 669.6/2).
split.fix: Use a criterion that depends on resistance and not on the HP ratio. Options: compare raw damage per bite (final_damage_amount on the wall) for stone and SC walls; compare share lost to 1/2 × (350/1500) × the stone share; or require lost_sc ≤ ½ lost_stone in absolute HP with a fixed number of attackers and fixed contact time.

votes.reasoning:
Я воспроизвёл измерения, но вывод находки не подтверждается. Заголовок преувеличен, а предложенные исправления неверны.

1. Мутация A подтверждается. Копия мода лежит в scratchpad/review/skeptic_tw. В data-final-fixes.lua дописано обнуление resistances у SC-стены и SC-ворот. Прогон: run.run('base', 8000, select=['combat']). Все 5 проверок T-W «SC-wall share» проходят, хотя SC-стены теряют больше очков прочности в абсолютных числах (у стен из камня цифры свои для каждого прогона):
   - coilgun: 2775,0 против 2415,2, проверка 0,01156 ≤ 0,02156;
   - gauss: 1035 против 705,6;
   - arc: 1230 против 827,6;
   - laser: 4680 против 4522.
   Механизм верный. Доля потерь = потеряно / (160 × max_health), поэтому проверка эквивалентна условию lost_sc ≤ 2,14 × lost_stone.

2. «Cannot fail» — неверно. Мутация B: max_health SC-стены = 350, стойкость прежняя. При ней T-W arc ПАДАЕТ: 0,010307 > 0,009404. У gauss запас тонкий: 0,00677 против 0,00705. Значит, проверка не пустая. Она чувствительна к прочности и к числу укусов, но не к стойкости.

3. Свойство, которое ломает мутация A, набор тестов уже ловит. W1 проверяет урон по каждому типу точными значениями: на мутанте 14 падений, например physical: получено 100 при ожидаемых 59,8. Так что пробела в покрытии нет. T-W по замыслу (R5, §11.6) — сценарий для совета о росте силы. Это не регресс-тест стойкости.

4. Критерий доли — принятое решение §15.2, и находка сама это признаёт. Код повторяет его дословно и с комментарием (combat.lua:833-835). Это претензия к решению спецификации, а не дефект теста.

5. Все три исправления из находки неверны:
   - Вариант 2 (доля ≤ ½ × 350/1500 × доля камня) алгебраически равен абсолютному критерию ≤ ½. Вариант 3 и есть абсолютный критерий.
   - Абсолютный критерий недостижим по самим числам спецификации. Укус в ванили (enemies.lua:25, 290, 351): средний жук — 15 physical, большой — 30.
     - Средний: камень (15−3)×0,8 = 9,6, SC (15−8)×0,65 = 4,55, отношение 0,47.

I tried to refute the finding and could not. I reproduced it.

**Code.** combat.lua:835-837 computes `lim = (stone_lost/stone_total)/2` and `frac = sc_lost/sc_total`. Both rings have 160 walls, at 350 HP (stone) and 1500 HP (SC). So the check is exactly `sc_lost <= 0.5*1500/350*stone_lost = 2.14*stone_lost`. The 4.29x HP ratio alone gives about 2.1x slack.

**Analysis from vanilla data.** /opt/factorio/data/base/prototypes/entity/enemies.lua: medium biter melee is 15 and big biter is 30. Damage per bite:
- stone wall (3/20%): 9.6 and 21.6
- SC wall with zero resistance: 15 and 30, which is 1.56x and 1.39x stone

Both are below 2.14x, so with a similar bite count a wall with no resistances still passes.

**Reproduction.** I made a scratch copy of the mod with every SC wall and SC gate resistance set to 0/0 (prototypes/spec_data.lua:989-997 and :1039-1047). I then ran only the combat module through tools/run.py (`run.MOD_SRC` set to the copy, base config, 9000 ticks, `--map-gen-seed 20260930`).

| | Original mod | Mutant (zero resistances) |
|---|---|---|
| Overall | 197 pass / 0 fail | 182 pass / 15 fail |
| Failing checks | none | 14 in W1, 1 in K10 |
| T-W SC checks | 5 of 5 pass | 5 of 5 pass |

Absolute wall HP lost by the mutant, SC vs stone:

| Turret | SC | Stone | Share check (got vs limit) |
|---|---|---|---|
| coilgun | 2775.0 | 2415.2 | 0.01156 vs 0.02156 |
| gauss | 1035.0 | 705.6 | 0.00431 vs 0.00630 |
| laser | 4680.0 | 4522.0 | passes |
| arc | 1230.0 | 827.6 | passes |
| gun | 10785 | 30884 | passes |

So the SC walls lose more absolute HP than stone walls, and the check still passes. My exact numbers differ slightly from the finding's (2655/2384.4). The conclusion is the same.

**Where the finding is overstated.**
- "Cannot fail" is too strong. The check fails if SC absolute loss exceeds 2.14x stone, for example if SC HP is cut. In practice it duplicates W2 (max HP) and does not respond to resistance or thorns.
- The mutation is caught elsewhere (W1, S4, K10). So "minor" is the right severity.

**Why it is still a real test defect.**
- The check is the only stated test of the §11 balance claim at FINAL_SPEC.md:993 ("SC-wall variants lose ≤ ½ of the stone-wall variants' wall HP"). R5 (line 716) relies on T-W to measure the effect.
- The §15.2 rationale is logically wrong. It says absolute loss "depends on the number of bites, not on resistance". But share = bites × damage per bite / (N × HP) is proportional to the bite count exactly as absolute loss is. Dividing by HP removes no bite-count dependence; it only adds a constant 4.29x credit.
- The change was made after pilots_combat.md §4 item 5 showed the absolute criterion fails. The pilot measured per-bite SC/stone ratios of 0.47 for medium and 0.66 for big biters, and listed three options: fixed seed with means over n≥5, a per-bite criterion for medium biters, or raising SC physical resistance to about 8/52%. §15.2 chose none of these. It chose a criterion that passes by construction. No record of this change exists in docs/council.
- With the committed results (tools/test_results.json), the absolute criterion fails:
  - base: coilgun 1136.2/2005.6 = 0.567, gauss 447.9/669.6 = 0.669
  - SA: coilgun 1229.8/2240.4 = 0.549, gauss 376.4/535.2 = 0.703

**On the finding's fix options.** Option 2 (share ≤ ½·(350/1500)·stone share) is algebraically the same as option 3 (absolute ≤ ½). Both will turn the suite red with the current mod. That is the honest result, but it is a design decision, not only a test edit.

  - `DOC`, transcribed by hand from the design spec;

  - the runtime export compared with the doc (`t_s4_doc`).

  Checking the same field against all four is deliberate cross-checking.

The facts in the finding check out, but the conclusion overstates them, and what remains does not count as a defect.

What checks out. I filtered tools/test_results.json by the cited names and got exactly 59 records, all pass=True, all counted in the 12,635 total. 1. 14 of the 59 are real checks that can fail, and they guard the rest of the suite.

Each is labelled "(справочно)" or "(информация)" in its own name and carries its value in `got`/`note`. They are 12 of 12,635, about 0.1% of the total. They do not touch the failure count, which is the number the verdict rests on. No mod bug is hidden and no outcome is wrong.

3. 'chain end X listed' (static.lua:931) and the E8 literal-length check (power.lua:337) are not tautologies about the mod. They check hand-typed tables: DOC is copied by hand from FINAL_SPEC, and static.lua:110 says "Не из spec.py" (not from spec.py). They fail on a copying typo, for example a chain end misspelled or missing from DOC.entities, in which case the next_upgrade = nil loop would silently skip it.
